classification_reasons: spec.md Flagged concerns leaves four items genuinely Open (risk-list hit, scope beyond the four named files, the git-fetch step-ordering prerequisite, and the shape of the reproducing test) with no decision recorded yet — not a tight spec.

blast radius: the plan targets six CI/CD workflow files that hold a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN and/or model secrets (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN) and gate the pipeline that controls production (sdlc.yaml deploy.production: true) — a risk_list hit ('production config') spec.md itself identifies.

no existing test exercises .github/workflows/*.yml; the reproducing-test shape (text-extract a step's run: block, execute it against a rigged git fixture) is new territory for this project, per spec.md's own Flagged concerns.
attempted: Intent: read intent.md's problem/outcome and compared against spec.md's Requirements/Design — the six-file scope (four named by the scan finding plus sdlc-test.yml/sdlc-deploy.yml found by this design pass) matches the intent's 'every other place with the same pattern'; no narrowing or drift found.

Spec and plan: checked spec.md Requirements against plan.md Files that change/Order of work — every requirement has a corresponding file and step; Open questions from intent are each answered with a traceable argument; Flagged concerns are explicitly left Open (expected at a human gate under profile: standard) rather than silently dropped.

Proof: this diff (phase b) is spec.md + plan.md + status.yaml + evidence only, no code; no test/build/lint logs exist yet and none are claimed — correct for a design-phase diff. Nothing here is the author's claim standing in for toolchain output.

Blast radius: read the diff (diff-b.patch) directly — it touches only changes/0008-security-supply-chain-sdlc-fix-yml-sdlc/{spec.md,plan.md,status.yaml,evidence/**}; no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) is touched. Read the six target workflow files plus sdlc-build.yml and sdlc-release.yml to check the design's factual claims against the real YAML: confirmed sdlc-fix.yml, sdlc-abandon.yml, sdlc-runbook.yml, sdlc-test.yml and sdlc-deploy.yml all check out an untrusted PR ref before or without a review gate and run `python .github/scripts/sdlc_pin.py` from that working tree, matching the design's account; confirmed sdlc-build.yml is gated on pull_request.merged == true (excluded correctly) and sdlc-release.yml already reads the script from a checkout pinned to merge_commit_sha (the template the design follows) — matches spec.md's Open questions #1 answer. One inaccuracy found: spec.md's Flagged concerns says 'the six workflows hold a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN' but sdlc-evals.yml's permissions block is contents: read only with no GITHUB_TOKEN in its env — only five of six hold a write-scoped token (the 'four of the six hold both model secrets' count is correct). This is a write-up imprecision in the risk narrative, not a change to which files need the fix or to the risk-list hit itself, and does not rise to REVIEW.md's Important bar (nothing behavior-breaking, no data leak, no policy breach) — noted, not escalated on.

Policies: security-baseline rule 6 (no eval/exec on external data) and rule 8 (risk-list hit needs accept-risk) are both cited correctly; coding-standards rule 5 (no new dependency) is honored by the text-extraction test design over a YAML-parsing library; no credential is quoted anywhere in spec.md, plan.md or evidence/hook-log.jsonl (checked directly, no .env read, no secrets_check deny).

Tests: none exist yet at this phase; plan.md commits to writing the reproducing test first (Order of work step 1) and never editing tests/test_calc.py or tests/test_flag.py — consistent with intent's Constraints and coding-standards rule 4. Nothing to weaken yet.
